clue.text: Old fellow at the station?

definitions.meaning: a railway station has ... at the end of the track to stop trains

explanation.surface: A question about an elderly man hanging about a railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: a fogeyish elderly man and the sprung stop at a track's end.

clue.text: Animal kept by uncultivated country child

parts.note: the bush is wild, uncleared land, as in Australia or Africa
a baby is a very young child

explanation.surface: Some creature is being looked after by a youngster from the wilds.
explanation.definitionFit: A bushbaby is a small nocturnal African primate, so it is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Appropriate to court of exalted king, since overthrown

indicators.note: a regime overthrown is toppled and turned upside down, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: R stands for Rex, Latin for king, the exalted ruler

explanation.surface: Something fits a royal court whose lofty monarch has since been deposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overthrown' shuffles OF, R and SINCE together; the king's court in the surface is really a court of law.
explanation.definitionFit: Forensic evidence or medicine is that used in or suitable to courts of law.

clue.text: Records doctor set up in Surrey

parts.note: EPs are extended-play records

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is lifted to read bottom to top

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

explanation.surface: Albums are being organised by a physician somewhere in Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns MO into OM. Surrey is a county just south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom is a town in the county of Surrey, famous for its racecourse and the Derby.

clue.text: Group is for capital punishment

annotationWithheld.why: 'Group is for capital punishment' as held: SCAFFOLD fits 'for capital punishment', but no parse of 'Group is' gives SCAFF or any other letters, and no source gives the setter's intent

clue.text: Stock owner can let charter lapse

indicators.note: a lapse is a slip or falling away from order, so these letters fall into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A shareholder is allowed to let a company's charter expire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' suggests shares; here it is livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock means livestock, so someone who owns a ranch of cattle is an owner of stock.

clue.text: Better provisions first discovered in soldier's hat

indicators.note: first says the provisions piece comes ahead of the other

parts.note: forage is food or fodder gathered as supplies
to cap something is to better or outdo it

explanation.surface: Improved supplies were found inside an infantryman's headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: A forage cap is a peaked cloth cap worn by soldiers off parade.

clue.text: Sort out the man inside with the rest

indicators.note: inside says one piece sits within the other
sorting something out puts it into a different order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: Settle things with the fellow in the room along with everybody else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' gives OTRS (the anagram of the word Sort); 'inside' signals the insertion. 'Sort out' reads as one phrasal verb but splits into fodder and indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Others means the remaining people or things, which is what the rest refers to.

clue.text: Moister type of Australian bread

definitions.meaning: a simple unleavened bread traditionally baked in campfire ashes in the outback

explanation.surface: A wetter kind of loaf from Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: One word serves as the comparative of damp and as the Australian bush bread baked in embers.

clue.text: Arranges penniless games

indicators.note: penniless means without a penny, and P is the abbreviation for penny

parts.note: sports are games

explanation.surface: Someone without money organises some games.
explanation.definitionFit: To sort things is to arrange or put them in order.

clue.text: Boy's back of leg under an overcoat

indicators.note: under places the leg piece after the boy's piece

parts.note: Peter is a boy's name, so the boy's gives Peter's
the ham is the back of the thigh

explanation.surface: A lad's hamstring is hidden beneath a heavy coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A petersham is a heavy overcoat, named after the 19th-century Viscount Petersham.

clue.text: Card games between banks?

parts.note: pontoon is a card game, the British name for blackjack
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: Games of cards played among financial institutions.
explanation.walkthrough: The banks are not money banks but the two sides of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A pontoon bridge floats on boats or drums and spans a river from one bank to the other.

clue.text: Using two names for Newton's generalised theorem about nitrogen

indicators.note: about says one piece goes around the other

parts.note: Isaac Newton generalised the binomial theorem
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Something named twice relates to a famous mathematical theorem applied to a gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Binominal describes the two-part naming system, genus plus species, used in biology.

clue.text: Buying or selling part of plant

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Trading in a portion of a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory; it is a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorse is a spiny yellow-flowered shrub, a common plant of heaths.

clue.text: Book by Victorian statesman on modern music

parts.note: John Bright was a Victorian radical politician
taken as written
rock is a modern style of music

explanation.surface: A volume written by a nineteenth-century politician about contemporary songs.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton rock is also a seaside sweet stick from Brighton, a resort on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton Rock is Graham Greene's 1938 novel, so it is a book.

clue.text: Water snake discovered in hot, empty river dwelling

indicators.note: discovered in says the pieces are found inside the other
empty removes the middle of the word, keeping only its first and last letters

parts.note: the Ouse is a river, a stretch of water
a boa is a large snake

explanation.surface: A water snake was spotted in a sweltering, deserted dwelling by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' and 'discovered in' are the indicators. 'Water' reads as part of a water snake, but it stands alone for the Ouse, an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: A houseboat is a boat fitted out to live on, so it is a home on a river.

clue.text: Descriptive of money wasted getting girl to shut up

parts.note: miss is a title or form of address for a girl
pent means confined or shut up, as in pent-up

explanation.surface: Squandered cash makes a girl go quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Money misspent is money wasted, so the word describes such money.

clue.text: Boss to order record of pedigree

parts.note: a boss is a raised knob or stud
to book is to order or reserve

explanation.surface: A manager tells someone to order a breeding register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' suggests a manager; it is a decorative knob.
explanation.definitionFit: A studbook records the pedigrees of thoroughbred animals, especially horses.

clue.text: Going round with cricketer when the course of events changed

definitions.text: when the course of events changed

parts.note: turning means rotating or going round
point is a cricket fielding position, and the fielder there

explanation.surface: Rotating alongside a cricket player at the moment history shifted.
explanation.walkthrough: Point is a fielder positioned square of the batsman on the off side in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A turning point is the moment at which a decisive change happens.

clue.text: Hazard hidden in garden

indicators.note: to hide is also to thrash, so a word hidden in a beating is knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A peril lurking among the flowerbeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden in' looks like a hidden-word signal, but GARDEN's letters are rearranged, not taken in a run.
explanation.definitionFit: Danger and hazard are synonyms for a risk of harm.

clue.text: The least important seat

explanation.surface: The lowliest place to sit.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest position in a ranking and a person's posterior share the same word.

clue.text: Only a novice unit

parts.note: L stands for learner, a novice driver's plate
one is a single unit

explanation.surface: Just one beginner on their own.
explanation.definitionFit: Alone can mean only, as in 'he alone knew'.

clue.text: Went over to see hares dancing in the grass

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

indicators.note: letters that dance move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone revisited a field to watch hares capering in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' gives HEARS (the anagram), and 'in' places it after the first two letters of the grass word; the 'the' before grass is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to go over something in practice, so rehearsed is went over.

clue.text: Cognac crated partly for African capital

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some brandy packed in boxes is bound for a city in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital city of Ghana in West Africa.

clue.text: Prepare to mend kettle, taking ages

definitions.meaning: fetch metal alloy for fixing a leaking pot

explanation.surface: Getting ready to fix the kettle takes forever.
explanation.walkthrough: Split one way it is fetching solder for a repair; split another it is ageing.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is fetching the alloy for a repair; read differently it means ageing.

clue.text: Belief that firm should be out of the red

indicators.note: the firm piece is placed outside the other, wrapping it

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
taken as written

explanation.surface: A conviction that a company ought to get out of debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of the red' suggests clearing debts; the company abbreviation simply goes round RED.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a creed or statement of belief.

clue.text: Sent money and relaxed

definitions.meaning: to remit is to send payment
to remit is also to ease or slacken

explanation.surface: Someone paid up and then calmed down.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both sending payment and easing off, as in remitting effort.

clue.text: Composer finding short title all right

parts.note: Bart is the short form of baronet, a hereditary title
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A musician finds an abbreviated honorific perfectly acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Bela Bartok was a Hungarian composer of the twentieth century.
